narrative.overview:
TicketAI is a professional tool that earns its invisibility. The interface is a neutral membrane between domain experts and their work — structured, unhurried, consistently dense without feeling crowded. Every primary aesthetic decision (Geist's geometric precision, the layered glass hierarchy, the single emerald accent) serves one purpose: keeping the expert focused on the ticket, not the interface itself.

The palette is deliberately restrained. Zinc-gray neutrals carry 90% of the screen; emerald enters only where it signals actionability or resolution — primary buttons, active navigation items, and validated-answer badges. This rarity is the point: when you see green, something is done or requires your action. Every other hue is strictly semantic.

Glass-morphism is structural rather than decorative. There is no animated background — the Aurora WebGL component was removed for legibility. Cards float above a clean #f9fafb page background via backdrop-filter blur, creating clear depth hierarchy without atmospheric distraction.
keyCharacteristics: Single-accent palette — emerald only, deployed with surgical precision
Glass as a structural depth signal, not an aesthetic statement
Geist Variable — one geometric family for all hierarchy levels
56px chrome (sidebar + navbar) maximizes vertical space for content
Semantic color system: emerald = validated/action · blue = processing · red = error · amber = count

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Emerald appears on at most 10–15% of any given screen. Its signal value depends entirely on scarcity. Never use it for decorative borders, hover effects unrelated to validation, or any non-action context.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: Geist Variable is the only typeface in the authenticated shell. Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono are login-page exceptions and must not cross that boundary.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Structural Rule
rules.body: Apply glass-card only to card-level containers that group a discrete unit of information. Nav elements, form fields, tooltips, and table rows are not cards.

rules.name: The Flat-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Sidebar and navbar use solid backgrounds (bg-white dark:bg-[#111113]), not glass. Chrome always recedes behind content.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Use rounded-md for interactive actions, rounded-xl for compact cards, rounded-2xl for large cards and dialogs. A button should never be rounder than the card it lives inside.

dos: Do use glass-card rounded-xl p-4 for compact cards and glass-card rounded-2xl p-5 for large dashboard cards.
Do deploy emerald exclusively on: primary action buttons, active nav items, validated/canonical status chips, and focus rings.
Do use text-xs font-semibold tracking-[0.06em] uppercase text-gray-400 for all sidebar section labels and stat card metric titles.
Do use transition-colors duration-150 on every interactive color change; duration-300 only for sidebar width collapse.
Do keep icons at 14–17px with strokeWidth 1.7–2.2. Small and precise — functional signals, not decorative glyphs.
Do use rounded-full only for pills (status chips), count badges, and circles (avatars, dots).
Do provide dark variants (dark:) for every color choice — dark mode is first-class.
donts: Don't use the login gradient (linear-gradient(100deg, #168B46, #2FE272)) or its emerald glow shadow inside the authenticated shell.
Don't render the Aurora WebGL component — removed for legibility.
Don't apply glass-card to nav elements, table rows, form fields, or tooltips. Glass signals a card-level container.
Don't apply rounded-2xl to buttons or inline nav items. That radius is reserved for large cards and dialogs.
Don't use blue as an action or brand color — blue appears only in the in-progress / processing semantic state.
Don't place more than one filled bg-emerald-600 button in a single view region. Ghost and icon variants absorb secondary actions.
Don't add extra shadow-* to glass-card containers — the glass token already includes its shadow vocabulary.
